text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT detected: multiple node flaps in us-west-2 serving pool. Symptom: gradual GPU memory creep on paged KV allocator -> OOMs and container restarts. Auto-escalation to incidents. (alert: paged_alloc_frag_rate > 0.8 for 18m)

dmitri: seeing same. nodes cycling every ~7-12m. error in logs: `CUDA out of memory` followed by `allocator: page_alloc failed` then container restart.

eva: adding initial blast radius: ~6 nodes, ~2% of total capacity for that pool, but spikes cause request queuing and 5xxs for heavy-chat models. Customers affected: a couple of mid-market tenants on Dedicated (billing tags: cust-A, cust-L).

sylvia: can we push a temporary mitigation? suggested: reduce paged-window to 512MB and force early eviction to lower resident set. Might cause perf regression but avoids OOM.

matt: +1 to forced eviction. Also let's throttle warmup and disable attention paging for models > 8k tokens for this pool. Command I ran locally to test eviction kick:
```
# kick eviction on node
redwood-runtime ctl mem-evict --pool us-west-2-paged --threshold 0.6
```

oncall-bot: runbook link: <https://internal/redwood/runbooks/paged-allocator#fast-mitigation>

dmitri: executed eviction command on two canaries. one node stabilized, nvtop shows steady GPU mem. but one node still creeping. logs show repeated small allocations pinned to same slab offsets -> possible fragmentation/sticky-resident pages.

sre-lead: prepare for rolling restart if eviction doesn't hold. Plan: cordon node -> drain pods -> restart runtime -> uncordon. Notify customers before rolling restart if we hit restart path.

customer-ops: flagged cust-A (ticket #INC-3421) and cust-L. ETA for update to both: 30m. cust-A experiencing 15% increase in error rate and 200ms added latency spikes.

eva: attaching heap/sample logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T02:12:04Z] alloc_patch: slab_id=42 offset=0x7f8b9f.. sticky_count=120 free_scan=0
[2026-03-15T02:12:05Z] kv_page_map: resident=94% frag=0.73 writes=124k
```

sylvia: hypothesis: background compaction didn't complete because page-ownership rotations are starving compactor due to continuous warmups. We should throttle warmup threads and increase compaction priority.

dmitri: implemented quick throttle: `redwood-runtime ctl warmup --pool us-west-2-paged --workers 2` and bumped compactor niceness. On canary node mem stabilized for 10m, fragmentation metric dropping slowly.

oncall-bot: NOTE: SLO guardrails: if error rate >10% for >10m escalate to SEV2. Current aggregated error rate for pool = 6.8% over last 5m.

sre-lead: good. continue canarying changes for another 20m. If creep resumes, schedule rolling restart of affected nodes in 10-min batches to avoid capacity cliff.

matt: logging a short-term code patch to allocator: reduce sticky retention window to 30s and add extra free-scan pass on eviction. Will create PR but won't merge without signoff (risk of perf regression). Patch ready in staging.

customer-ops: update sent to cust-A and cust-L: "We are mitigating a memory fragmentation issue in the paged KV allocator. Expect transient errors as we stabilize; dedicated capacity may be impacted. We'll notify if rolling restarts start." (reaction :white_check_mark:)

eva: after 35m of these mitigations two nodes still showed creep; we kicked rolling restart on those two. Post-restart: both nodes back to stable memory patterns and no further OOMs for 25m.

dmitri: follow-ups: enable longer-term fixes: 1) compactor tuning to run opportunistically during warmup, 2) more aggressive free-scan when fragmentation > 0.6, 3) add metric to detect sticky-resident slab count. I'll open issues and link PR.

sre-lead: handoff summary for next on-call: root cause likely combination of sticky-resident allocations + compaction starvation during constant warmup traffic. Live mitigations applied: eviction kicks, warmup throttle, compactor priority bump, two targeted rolling restarts. Customer impact: limited (cust-A ~15% errors briefly), no major revenue impact. Next actions: follow-up PRs, longer-term allocator fixes, add automated preemptive eviction when frag trend rising. On-call takeaways: prefer eviction + throttle before rolling restarts if customers can tolerate short perf hit.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT resolved -> monitoring for 2h. If metrics deviate, reopen. Autoclose in 2h.

sylvia: adding tickets: ALLOC-1273 (compaction tuning), ALLOC-1274 (sticky-resident metric), ALLOC-1275 (safe shrink policy). will assign to eng-runtime.

matt: thanks team. handing off to next oncall @dmitri for follow-ups."
